label: prop:double-slit-massive-pattern
title: Massive-particle interference pattern
html:
Let \alpha be a massive q-harmonic form (particle) incident on a double slit. The q-deformed intensity at scattering angle \theta is

  I_q(\theta)
  =  4I_0\cos^2\!\!\left(\frac{\Delta\Phi_q(\theta)}{2}\right)
        \cdot
        \left(\frac{\sin\beta_q(\theta)}{\beta_q(\theta)}\right)^{\!2}.

The interference phase is

  \Delta\Phi_q(\theta)
  =  q^{-1}\frac{2\pi d\sin\theta}{\lambda}
        +  (1 - q^{-1})\Delta\phi_\xi(\theta).

The envelope parameter is

  \beta_q(\theta)
  =  q^{-1}\frac{\pi a\sin\theta}{\lambda}
        +  (1 - q^{-1})^2\beta_\xi(\theta).

The term \beta_\xi(\theta) is the spin-core contribution of the q-Laplacian expansion.

The q-Laplacian separates into three scales:

  • Classical core (\propto q^{-2}): Standard Hodge diffusion \Delta.
  • Spin core (\propto (1 - q^{-1})^2): Pure Reeb dynamics \Delta_\xi.
  • Cross-coupling (\propto q^{-1}(1 - q^{-1})): Mixes spatial and Reeb modes.

The fringe spacing is

  \Delta y_q =  \frac{q\lambda L}{d}.

The envelope half-width broadens:

  w_q =  \frac{q^2\lambda L}{a}
        \left(1 +  (1 - q^{-1})^2
        \frac{\langle\Delta_\xi\rangle}{\langle\Delta\rangle}\right).

At q = 1, this recovers the classical Fraunhofer pattern. In the 600\;\mathrm{eV} single-electron double-slit buildup experiment of Roger Bach, Damian Pope, Sy-Hwang Liou, and Herman Batelaan [bach2013] (a = 50\;\mathrm{nm}, d = 280\;\mathrm{nm}, relativistic \lambda_{\mathrm{dB}} \approx 50.05\;\mathrm{pm}, 6{,}235 electrons across the central five interference orders), an electrostatic quadrupole lens magnifies the pattern without an independent angular scale bar, making the dimensionless envelope-to-fringe ratio w_q / \Delta y_q \ge q(d/a) and the order-m peak modulation I_q(\theta_m)/I_q(0) = \mathrm{sinc}^2(m\pi a / (q d)) the magnification-invariant observables. Under the local vacuum profile q_{\mathrm{local}}(y) \to 1, the aperture-averaged departure \langle q_{\mathrm{local}} - 1 \rangle_a \le 1.70 \times 10^{-6} across a = 50\;\mathrm{nm} agrees with q = 1 Fraunhofer to better than 8.1 \times 10^{-6} pointwise and predicts I(\theta_{\pm 2})/I(0) = \mathrm{sinc}^2(5\pi/14) \approx 0.6448 against the digitized Figure 3e mean m = \pm 2 peak height 0.6552 (1.58\% difference), whereas a uniform exterior q = q_0 \approx 1.1100 would lift I_{q_0}(\theta_{\pm 2})/I_{q_0}(0) to 0.7026 and stretch the physical fringe spacing \Delta\theta_{q_0} = q_0\lambda_{\mathrm{dB}}/d by +11.00\%.
